headline: A strong storm brings rain and northeast gusts up to about 40–45 mph around Charlotte and the region early Thanksgiving under a Wind Advisory until 10 AM, then winds pick back up from the southwest Thursday afternoon and a cold, breezy Friday follows before a milder weekend.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Rain spreads across the region early Thanksgiving morning, staying all rain, and lingers through at least daybreak, possibly into mid-morning east of the mountains including Charlotte. Northeast winds are already gusting up to 40 mph and the Wind Advisory runs until 10 AM; gusts likely top out near 45 mph away from the highest peaks but can blow over holiday decorations, tents, canopies and outdoor cookers (keep a fire extinguisher handy) and cause a few power outages. Winds drop off for a while late morning into early afternoon as the storm passes to the east, then turn southwest and become gusty again Thursday afternoon and night, with low clouds hanging on through early evening. Rain totals have trended down and the flood risk is low (a Marginal, level 1 of 4, risk), aside from some poor-drainage flooding where leaves clog storm drains, mainly along and east of I-77; Thursday evening, rain wrapping around the storm turns to snow showers along the Tennessee border.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Snow showers near the Tennessee border Thursday night into Friday should add up to an inch or less, while areas east of the mountain crest most likely stay dry. Friday is cold, about 10 degrees below normal, feeling like a typical winter day, with frequent west to southwest gusts of 25 to 35 mph lasting until around sunset, below advisory level, and a gray low-cloud deck possibly lingering; breezy conditions continue into Friday night. Saturday turns dry and quieter under high pressure with temperatures warming back to normal.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A strong storm passes well to the northwest across the Midwest and Great Lakes Sunday into Monday morning, sending a weakening cold front through Sunday afternoon into Sunday night or early Monday with a brief shot of rain. Rain chances may run somewhat higher than some guidance shows, but amounts should stay under a quarter inch everywhere except southwest North Carolina. Temperatures stay near normal from Monday onward.

watch_for: Wind gusts up to 40–45 mph until 10 AM Thursday — secure decorations, tents and outdoor cookers
Renewed southwest gusts of 25–35 mph Thursday afternoon through Friday
Snow showers near the Tennessee border Thursday evening into Friday, with up to an inch possible
confidence: Forecasters say the storm is behaving as expected and the overall scenario is on track, with a low flood risk unless the storm's track shifts west; the weekend and early next week look relatively quiet.
